title: Start dancing Kizomba TODAY! Dance tutorial for beginners

observation_window.sampling: provider default; not continuous motion capture

extraction.teacher_style: The teacher provides clear, step-by-step instructions with a focus on body mechanics and posture. She uses simple, relatable analogies to help students understand the nuances of the dance.

lesson_structure.note: The teacher introduces the basic stance in Kizomba.
The teacher explains the roles of the leader and follower.
The teacher breaks down the first basic step.
The teacher practices the first basic step with music.
The teacher breaks down the second basic step.
The teacher practices the second basic step with music.
The teacher breaks down the third basic step.

cues: weight on the ball of your foot
keep your body in a neutral position
metaphors: waiting in line at the grocery store
common_mistakes: bringing the balls of your feet up
pushing your body parts to the side
safety: keep your knees relaxed with a soft bend

steps_taught.name: Basic 1
steps_taught.description: A basic step with feet together, shifting weight from one foot to the other.

steps_taught.name: Basic 2
steps_taught.description: A side-to-side step with a weight shift and a mark.

steps_taught.name: Basic 3
steps_taught.description: A forward and backward step with a mark.

what_hinders: the teacher's fast pace in some segments

quotes.text: all your body parts under you
your weight is going to be on the ball of your foot
think about it as if you were waiting in line
in Kizomba, the energy goes down
marca means you're coming together and you're resetting

evidence_segments.observation: The teacher stands in front of the camera and explains the basic stance.
The teacher shows a couple dancing to illustrate the roles of the leader and follower.
The teacher demonstrates the first basic step.
The teacher demonstrates the first basic step from the back.
The teacher demonstrates the second basic step.

extraction.distinctive_method: The teacher emphasizes the importance of keeping the energy down and avoiding any tapping, which is a common feature in other dance styles.
